title: PiPedal Bluetooth MIDI reconnect
problem: After a Bluetooth MIDI controller is powered off and on, ALSA announces the client before its port exists; PiPedal tries to reconnect too early and ignores the later port announcement.
reproduce: Start PiPedal with an M-VAVE Chocolate connected, power the controller off and on, then observe that aconnect lists it without a connection to PiPedal until pipedald restarts.
acceptance: Client-start and port-start announcements both trigger idempotent configuration refresh, the later port event finds the saved stable port ID, no daemon restart is needed, and existing MIDI input behavior remains unchanged.
repair: Forward ALSA port-start events through the existing device-added callback so saved sequencer connections are applied after the recreated port becomes enumerable.

verification.limitations: BCL deterministically checks the event-order policy and production callback wiring. AlsaSequencer.cpp also passes a C++20 syntax build against ALSA 1.2.14 in Debian; this case does not emulate the ALSA sequencer kernel or Bluetooth hardware.
verification.ownerCheck: On the Raspberry Pi from issue #472, start with the M-VAVE Chocolate connected, power it off until it disappears from aconnect -l, then power it on. Confirm aconnect shows it connected to PiPedal and preset/snapshot switching works without restarting pipedald. Repeat three times and record PiPedal, kernel and BlueZ versions.
